Possession-based player rates

Source: R/rates.R
player_rates.Rd

The rate statistics of modern analysis, with Basketball-Reference definitions. They put players from teams (and leagues) with different pace and game length on the same footing:

Usage

player_rates(players, teams, ft_coef = 0.44)

Arguments

players

Player season totals (minutes, pts, p2a, p3a, fta, tov, orb, drb, ast, stl, blk; optionally p2m, p3m) with team and, if present, league and season.

teams

Team totals with opponent columns (o_ prefix), as in team_seasons; min = total player minutes.

ft_coef

Free-throw weight in possessions (0.44).

Value

players with the rate columns added.

Details

  • ts_pct: true shooting, points per shooting possession, PTS / (2 (FGA + 0.44 FTA)).

  • usg_pct: share of team possessions a player uses while on the floor.

  • tov_pct: turnovers per 100 plays (FGA + 0.44 FTA + TOV).

  • orb_pct, drb_pct: share of available rebounds grabbed on the floor.

  • stl_pct: steals per opponent possession on the floor.

  • blk_pct: share of opponent 2-point attempts blocked on the floor.

  • ast_pct: share of teammates' baskets assisted on the floor (only when player makes p2m, p3m are available).

  • efg_pct: effective FG% (also needs makes).

All are returned as proportions (0.25, not 25).

Examples

pr <- player_rates(player_seasons, team_seasons)
head(pr[order(-pr$usg_pct), c("player", "usg_pct", "ts_pct")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   player           usg_pct ts_pct
#>   <chr>              <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Achille Lonati     0.611  0    
#> 2 Declan Duru        0.502  0    
#> 3 Joseba Querejeta   0.458  0.333
#> 4 James Wiseman      0.426  0.615
#> 5 Tyrone Wallace     0.377  0.364
#> 6 LaMelo Ball        0.361  0.536
